title: Chemical Changes: Definitions of Reaction Types
subject: Science

questions.question: Which statement best defines a combustion reaction?
options: A reaction where a substance breaks down into simpler substances when heated
A reaction where a substance reacts with oxygen and releases thermal energy and light
A reaction where an acid reacts with an alkali to form a salt and water
A reaction where a metal reacts with water to produce hydrogen gas
questions.explanation: Combustion is a reaction with oxygen that releases thermal energy. Examples include burning fuels, magnesium ribbon in air, or cellular respiration.

questions.question: Which statement best defines thermal decomposition?
options: A reaction where two substances combine to form one product
A reaction where a single substance breaks down into simpler substances when heated
A reaction where a metal reacts with oxygen to form an oxide
A reaction where an acid neutralises an alkali
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition means 'breaking down by heat'. One reactant breaks into two or more products when thermal energy is supplied.

questions.question: Which statement best defines an oxidation reaction?
options: A reaction where a substance gains oxygen
A reaction where a substance loses oxygen
A reaction that only occurs at high temperatures
A reaction that produces a salt and water
questions.explanation: Oxidation involves gaining oxygen. At Sec 2 level, students learn oxidation as 'reaction with oxygen'.

questions.question: Which statement best defines a neutralisation reaction?
options: A reaction where a metal reacts with an acid to produce hydrogen gas
A reaction where an acid reacts with an alkali to produce a salt and water
A reaction where a carbonate reacts with an acid to produce carbon dioxide
A reaction where two metals combine to form an alloy
questions.explanation: Neutralisation is when an acid reacts with an alkali to form a salt and water.

questions.question: Which reaction type always requires oxygen as a reactant?
questions.explanation: Combustion always involves a substance reacting with oxygen.

questions.question: Which reaction type has only one reactant?
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition has a single reactant that breaks down into two or more products when heated.

questions.question: Rusting of iron is an example of which type of chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: Rusting is oxidation: iron reacts with oxygen and water to form rust.

questions.question: Which reaction type produces a salt and water as products?
questions.explanation: Neutralisation always produces a salt and water.

questions.question: Heating calcium carbonate to produce calcium oxide and carbon dioxide is an example of:
questions.explanation: This is thermal decomposition: one reactant breaks down into two products when heated.

questions.question: Which statement is true about all four reaction types?
options: They all require heat to start
They all involve the formation of new substances
They all involve oxygen as a reactant
questions.explanation: All chemical reactions involve the formation of new substances with different properties from the reactants.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of combustion?
options: Calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide
Hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride + water
questions.explanation: Combustion is a reaction with oxygen that releases thermal energy and often light. Magnesium burning in air to form magnesium oxide is a combustion reaction.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of thermal decomposition?
options: Hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride + water
Calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition is when a single substance breaks down into simpler substances when heated.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of neutralisation?
options: Calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide
Hydrochloric acid + potassium hydroxide → potassium chloride + water
questions.explanation: Neutralisation is when an acid reacts with an alkali to produce a salt and water.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of oxidation?
options: Calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide
Hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride + water
questions.explanation: Oxidation is a reaction with oxygen. Zinc reacting with oxygen to form zinc oxide is an oxidation reaction.

questions.question: Cellular respiration is an example of which reaction type?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration is an oxidation reaction where glucose reacts with oxygen to release thermal energy.

questions.question: Photosynthesis is the opposite of which reaction type?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and produces oxygen. Cellular respiration (an oxidation reaction) uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide. They are essentially opposite processes.

questions.question: Which reaction type involves breaking down a compound using heat?
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition means 'breaking down by heat'. One reactant breaks into two or more products when thermal energy is supplied.

questions.question: Which reaction type releases thermal energy and often produces light?
questions.explanation: Combustion is a reaction with oxygen that releases thermal energy and often produces light (flame).

questions.question: Which reaction type involves an acid and an alkali?
questions.explanation: Neutralisation is when an acid reacts with an alkali to produce a salt and water.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares combustion and oxidation?
options: Combustion is rapid oxidation with a flame; oxidation can be rapid or slow
Oxidation always produces a flame; combustion does not
Combustion and oxidation are completely different reaction types
Oxidation only occurs in living things; combustion only occurs in engines
questions.explanation: Combustion is a type of oxidation that is rapid and produces a flame. Oxidation is the broader category: it can be rapid (burning) or slow (rusting, respiration). Both involve reaction with oxygen.
